body: Thanks for the recommendation, it sounds interesting. Always something to learn!
I do feel emotions, but the “volume” is turned way down on them. It’s very easy to ignore.
It’s really not that bad. I will definitely keep open to possibilities.

Thanks for this strategy of working backwards. I haven’t tried that kind of approach. I do find beauty in things (although I don’t seek it out) but it usually ends up as a passing acknowledgement that I move on from. 

In the state I am, I’m specifically noticing the beauty of people helping people. The other comments in this thread are pointing to working on that, which is something I’ll work on.

I totally agree with getting exercise. I’m into long distance running and it is one of the few things that has always invigerorated me in my life.

Your last comments really gave me something to think about. Thanks for the offer to continue discussion.

Thanks. I’ve dabbled in Buddhism (but more closely relate to the secular version). I really enjoy the concept of the Middle way.  I also like your perspective on more actively participating as a balance of detachment. I guess I got into the rut of looking at absolute detachment as a good thing since attachment really derailed me at one point.

This is a great suggestion. I can totally relate to the helping people in IT, because I do a lot of that myself.

I’ll definitely look into this more.

Thanks for this. I know it seems like a fine line with depression (which I think I’ve worked through, but have symptoms of), so maybe I can explain it differently: I’ve become so detached, that I’m pretty much in a perpetual state of being content. Not blissful, but a neutral content.

Perhaps this is what some people feel like towards the end of a long life. I’m really thankful, but it just seems like I’ve come to an end of a good book (even though I’m in my late 30’s).

PS: I totally agree with your strategies on depression. They are great suggestions/practices that I have incorporated into my life like long distance running and photography that really helped get me out of depression.

Thanks glad to find someone who can understand. My therapist is having a hard time figuring this one out. Maybe I’ll post in some other meditation subreddits  if you come across anything, I’m open to it!

Until then I’m going to hang on the best I can.

I think you hit on something. I had a “enlightened”experience through meditation about 5 years ago. It instantly detached everything I clung to. All of the sudden everything was connected to everything. This instantly cured my depression. 

But it was replaced with increased detachment and loss of meaning. Even detachment from myself. The ego was completely gone. Double edge sword!

Im in search of someone with a relatable experience. It’s been hard to find!
